headline: AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D drops to $279 days after launch
summary: The new mid-range X3D chip is now available for significantly less than its MSRP, making it a compelling gaming option.
details: AMD's Ryzen 7 7700X3D, initially priced at $329, has seen a substantial price drop to $279 through a Newegg promo code. This discount significantly improves its value proposition for gamers.
The Ryzen 7 7700X3D is an 8-core, 16-thread processor with 104MB of cache and a 120W TDP, similar to the higher-end 7800X3D. Its boost clock reaches 4.5 GHz.

While the 7800X3D offers a slightly higher boost clock and marginally better gaming performance, the $120 price difference at $279 makes the 7700X3D a more sensible choice for budget-conscious gamers.

For productivity tasks, Intel's latest Arrow Lake refresh chips may offer better performance. However, for gaming-focused builds, the discounted Ryzen 7 7700X3D presents a strong value on the AM5 socket.

The Ryzen 7 7700X3D is a Newegg exclusive in North America until Q4 2026, explaining its rapid discounting. This deal is ideal for those looking to enter the X3D ecosystem without exceeding a $300 budget.

headline_marked: [[RTX 3080]] cooled by 11 fans and AIO drops 30°C, gains just 2 FPS
headline: RTX 3080 cooled by 11 fans and AIO drops 30°C, gains just 2 FPS
summary: A wild modder strapped 11 fans and a 360mm AIO cooler to an RTX 3080, slashing temps by nearly half but only boosting frame rates by a measly 2 FPS.
details: One PC modder, TrashBench, decided to see how far they could push an Nvidia RTX 3080 by adding extra fans, duct tape, and cable ties. The goal was to see if reduced temperatures from boosted airflow would result in more frames per second.
After cleaning and repasting the Asus ROG RTX 3080, the baseline temperature during stress testing was 70°C. With the stock cooler's fans at 100%, this dropped to 63°C.

Replacing the stock shroud with three Arctic case fans brought the GPU temperature down to a stable 52°C. Swapping these for thicker server fans, with added duct tape to prevent air leakage, further reduced temps to 50°C, though a subsequent attempt with duct tape resulted in a warmer 54°C.

Adding five tiny Arctic server fans running at up to 15,000 RPM along the top of the card, creating a jet-engine-like sound, did not significantly improve temperatures, keeping the RTX 3080 from holding below 50°C for extended periods.

The experiment took a turn with the addition of backplate fans, but the real breakthrough came when an AiO 360mm cooler was integrated. This setup achieved a new best, with the GPU reporting a stable top temperature of just 41°C in the Unigine Heaven benchmark.

Despite the dramatic temperature reduction, performance gains were minimal. Benchmark runs in Shadow of the Tomb Raider showed only modest uplifts, even when taking advantage of the newfound overclocking headroom. The modder concluded that the mod, while looking and sounding 'awesome' and nearly halving temperatures, was not worth the effort for just a 2 FPS increase.
